rules.reason: A person starts the task in a conversation and reviews the result, so it is a client skill.
It is one person's own recurring task, done as them, so it is a Claude Code scheduled task.

Shared team work that runs on a schedule and lives in Slack is a Claude Tag channel routine. Keeping it to internal and confidential data is our choice, because page 10 allows Claude Tag for those classes only; it is not used under ZDR, which turns Claude Tag off, or when the customer requires self-hosting.
Work wired into systems that holds PHI has no hosted agent runtime: Managed Agents is blocked under HIPAA readiness, and whether the Agent SDK is covered is Unverified.
What would start the task on an escalation is Unverified, so the manager starts it in a conversation until that is confirmed.
The customer wants work that runs without a person on its own infrastructure, and Managed Agents can be self-hosted, so it runs on a self-hosted Managed Agents deployment.

A scheduled job wired into systems that needs ZDR cannot use hosted Managed Agents, which is not ZDR-eligible, so it runs on a fully self-hosted Managed Agents deployment, one of the page's two ZDR routes (the other is the Messages API with eligible features).
Work wired into systems with no ZDR or HIPAA need runs on Managed Agents.

A client skill runs as the signed-in user: their own permissions, with connectors each person signs in to. A connector whose page-11 row says otherwise (Intercom acts as the admin who authorized it; Dynamics uses a custom Entra app) is listed in connectors[], where its identity is checked against that row.
A Claude Code scheduled task appears as the user, with all their connectors.
A Claude Tag routine acts as a service account, so it survives turnover.
Managed Agents acts with an API key plus a per-user vault of credentials, not a user's sign-in.
The Agent SDK acts with your API key plus credentials you pass in. api-key-vault is the nearest value we have, our choice: the build keeps those credentials in a vault.
No runtime is allowed for this task, so it has no identity; our choice, the value is null.
Every task starts at level 1 and earns each level with evidence from evals.
Undecided: page 06 sets the ceiling from audience, reversibility, money, deletes and trigger, but has no rule for a high cost of a mistake, so a person must decide it.
The output reaches someone outside the company, so the task stays at level 1 or 2.
The task touches money, so it stays at level 1 or 2.
The task deletes, so it stays at level 1 or 2.

The action cannot be undone and its output leaves the team. Page 06 lets a task above level 2 only when it can be undone or is internal, and we treat another team as not internal, our choice, so it stays at level 1 or 2.
The task reads untrusted input next to a send, so a person approves each post and it stays at level 2.
The task shares a connector tool with a task whose ceiling is lower, so both run at the stricter task's level.
No rule on page 06 caps this task lower, so it may rise to level 3 once evals support it; a person starts it, so not to unattended level 4.
No rule on page 06 caps this task lower, so it may rise to level 3 once evals support it; a person starts it until the event source is confirmed, so it may not run unattended.
No rule on page 06 caps this task lower, so it may rise to unattended level 4 once evals support it.
A managed settings file is read by Claude Code on a device, and a hosted runtime runs on no user's device, so there is no settings baseline to set; our reading of page 13.
Claude Tag runs in Slack, not on a device, so the managed settings file that Claude Code reads does not apply to it; our reading of page 13.
With no device management the twin lives in claude.ai on the web, which has no managed settings file.

Highly sensitive work needs the controls page 10 requires for it (org lock via MDM, a sandbox that fails closed, allowlists, redaction hooks), and the industry pack's settings baseline is where we keep them; our choice. A pack with no baseline leaves this undecided.
PHI work in Claude Code needs the HIPAA managed settings.
Confidential data needs managed deny rules, a sandbox and telemetry off: the confidential baseline.
Internal data takes the baseline managed settings: the general baseline.
Web search and fetch are not allowed for this data class: queries can reveal intent.
Page 10 lists web fetch as not allowed for PHI, and lists web search as eligible only for the API route, so we keep both off until the customer's HIPAA configuration is confirmed; our choice.
Web tools are allowed for this data class.
A hosted runtime runs on no user's device, so no Claude client surface is allowed for it. Any front end page 13 names (a web page behind SSO, or a Teams or Slack bot) is ours to build; our reading.
A Claude Tag routine runs in Slack.
This data class runs in Claude Code on a managed device, locked by MDM, and not in Desktop. On a mixed fleet this is the managed share's surface; the unmanaged share gets no direct access.
This data class gets no direct access from an unmanaged device.
Confidential data on an unmanaged device is for claude.ai on the web only.
Internal data on an unmanaged device is for claude.ai on the web and Desktop, through SSO.
On a managed device every surface the role works in is allowed, with managed settings.
Highly sensitive deal work keeps zero data retention.
Retention passes the customer's own compliance.retention setting through; our choice, as the page states no rule for it. Warnings say where that setting falls short for the task.
Personal memory is not wanted on this card, so role knowledge stays in skills and memory is off. Memory on claude.ai is one org-wide switch, so this is what we recommend for the org; our choice.

The task reads untrusted input. Memory on claude.ai is one org-wide switch, so a per-task 'off' is a build instruction, not a setting: the task's skill writes nothing to memory, and only controlled steps write it. Our choice, from page 02's advice on memory poisoning.

Personal memory is wanted and the task reads no untrusted input, so memory may be on for it. Memory on claude.ai is one org-wide switch, so this says only that the task does not need it off; our choice.

The task runs as the signed-in user, so each connector acts through that user's own sign-in. A connector whose page-11 row says otherwise (Intercom acts as the admin who authorized it; Dynamics uses a custom Entra app) is listed in connectors[], where its identity is checked against that row; our choice.
In a channel Claude Tag acts as its own service account.
Managed Agents acts with an API key plus a per-user vault of credentials.
The Agent SDK acts with your API key plus credentials you pass in. api-key-vault is the nearest value we have, our choice: the build keeps those credentials in a vault.
No runtime is allowed for this task, so its connectors have no identity; our choice, the value is null.
Reading is allowed at every level.

The task reads untrusted content and can send it out, so a person approves each send.
Individual plans are not for company data; Team is the minimum.

PHI needs a dedicated HIPAA org with a signed BAA, which needs Enterprise.
PHI runs only in a dedicated HIPAA org, where connectors and skills are not covered by the BAA.
Highly sensitive data needs a separate Enterprise org with ZDR.

With no allowlisting and no MCP tunnel on this plan, the private system is reachable only from something running inside the network: Claude Code on a device there (a local MCP server), or a self-hosted runtime deployed there; our reading of page 11's routes.
The private network is reached through an MCP tunnel: Enterprise, by request, a research preview with no SLA.
A self-hosted Managed Agents deployment runs from a Platform (API) org besides the people's org, as page 14's org plan does for private equity; we apply that plan here, our choice.
This customer can allowlist Anthropic's IP range, so the private network is reachable at the edge.
The Zendesk connection is in early access and which Claude plans it supports is Unverified.
Confidential data is acceptable on Team only where the audit need is lower, so the fit has limits.
Highly sensitive data needs a separate Enterprise org with ZDR (qualified orgs, Claude Code only); confirm the customer has one.
The data class is allowed on this plan.

On Team an Owner shares skills and plugins to everyone; group targeting needs Enterprise.
This plan cannot publish plugins to users, so users install them by hand.
Claude.ai on the web with no device management takes no managed settings file, so there is no baseline.
PHI work needs the HIPAA managed settings.

Highly sensitive work needs the controls page 10 requires for it (org lock via MDM, a sandbox that fails closed, allowlists, redaction hooks), and the industry pack's settings baseline is where we keep them; our choice. A pack with no baseline leaves this undecided.
The role handles confidential data: the confidential baseline.
The role handles internal data only: the general baseline.
The customer is on an individual plan, which gives IT no control and uses consumer terms; Team is the minimum for company data.
rules.fix: Move the role's users onto a Team or Enterprise plan before the twin is built.

rules.reason: The customer requires a log of every action, and the twin runs where no governance hook can run (claude.ai on the web, no device management).
rules.fix: Run the twin in Claude Code on MDM-managed devices with the governance hook locked in managed settings, or agree with the customer to drop the requirement.

rules.reason: The task is highly sensitive, and this plan has no Enterprise org with ZDR.
rules.fix: Set up a separate Enterprise org with ZDR for this work, or lower the task's data class with the customer's compliance owner.

rules.reason: The task is highly sensitive or PHI and would run on an unmanaged device, which gets no direct access.
rules.fix: Give these users managed devices, or run a hosted twin on our infrastructure that the device only displays.

rules.reason: PHI is in scope, and there is no dedicated HIPAA org with a signed BAA.
rules.fix: Set up a dedicated HIPAA org on Enterprise with a signed BAA, or take PHI out of the role's tasks.

rules.reason: The PHI task needs a hosted runtime, and page 10 reads its lists as giving none for PHI: Managed Agents is blocked under HIPAA readiness, and whether the Agent SDK is covered is Unverified.
rules.fix: Make it a task a person starts in Claude Code under the HIPAA configuration, or wait until Anthropic confirms a hosted route in writing.

rules.reason: The task reads a system on a private network and runs on an Anthropic-hosted runtime (Claude Tag or Managed Agents) that cannot reach it on this plan: no MCP tunnel and no allowlisting.
rules.fix: Allowlist Anthropic's IP range 160.79.104.0/21 at the edge, move the job to a runtime inside the network (Claude Code there, or a self-hosted deployment), or move to Enterprise for an MCP tunnel.

rules.reason: The task writes to Gmail or Google Calendar, whose directory connectors read only: they cannot create, send or change mail or events.
rules.fix: End the task in a draft that a person sends, and remove the write from the card.

rules.reason: The task needs ZDR cover, and whether the Agent SDK is covered is Unverified, so the plan uses self-hosted Managed Agents, the route the page confirms.
rules.fix: Keep the Agent SDK out of this task until Anthropic confirms its ZDR cover in writing.

rules.reason: The task runs on the Agent SDK and needs ZDR or HIPAA cover, and whether the Agent SDK is covered is Unverified.
rules.fix: Get Anthropic's written confirmation of the cover, or move the task to a route the pages confirm.

rules.reason: The role plugin is shared to everyone; group targeting needs Enterprise.
rules.fix: Keep the role plugin free of anything other roles must not see, or move to Enterprise.

rules.reason: Claude.ai on the web with no device management gets no managed settings and no hooks.
rules.fix: Put the guardrails in connector tool permissions and skills, and tell the customer what cannot be locked.

rules.reason: The governance log is a Claude Code hook, so a twin on the web has none.
rules.fix: Record use from the usage dashboard and the source systems' own audit, and say so in the design.

rules.reason: This plan has no audit log and no Compliance API.
rules.fix: Rely on the source systems' own audit logs, or move to Enterprise.

rules.reason: Confidential data on Team is acceptable only where the audit need is lower.
rules.fix: Confirm with the customer's compliance owner that the lower audit need holds.

rules.reason: Confidential data on an unmanaged device calls for read-only connectors, and the task writes; on a mixed fleet this holds for the people on unmanaged devices.
rules.fix: Make the task's connectors read-only for people on unmanaged devices (set the write tools to Blocked), or have the customer accept the write in writing.

rules.reason: The task sends email or puts an event on a calendar through Gmail or Google Calendar, and both directory connectors read only, so the task ends in a draft a person sends.
rules.fix: Write the skill so it ends with a draft in the conversation that the person copies and sends, or adds to the calendar.

rules.reason: A system on a private network must be reachable from Anthropic's IP range, allowlisted at the edge.
rules.fix: Have the customer allowlist 160.79.104.0/21 at the edge before the task is built.

rules.reason: Claude Tag on confidential data belongs only in scoped private channels.
rules.fix: Run the routine in a private channel limited to the team.

rules.reason: Whether the Slack directory connector can post is Unverified; post through Claude Tag or the Slack MCP server.
rules.fix: Post through Claude Tag or the Slack MCP server, not the directory connector.

rules.reason: The task reads untrusted content and can send it out, so a person approves each send.
rules.fix: Set the send tool to Needs approval and keep the task at level 2 or below.

rules.reason: The task reads untrusted input while personal memory is wanted. Memory on claude.ai is one org-wide switch, so it cannot be turned off for this task alone: the task's skill must write nothing to memory, and only controlled steps write it.
rules.fix: Keep role knowledge in reviewed skills and build the task so it never writes memory; if the org cannot keep memory writes to controlled steps, ask the Owner to switch memory off org-wide.

rules.reason: Nothing confirmed can start the task on its event, so a person starts it until that is confirmed.
rules.fix: Confirm with Anthropic and the vendor what would fire the event, then level the task again.

rules.reason: The task's connector is in an early-access programme, with Unverified points.
rules.fix: Confirm the connection's plan support and per-user checks with the vendor before the build.

rules.reason: The HubSpot connector needs approval from a HubSpot Super Admin (or a user with App Marketplace access) as well as an Owner.
rules.fix: Name the customer's HubSpot Super Admin, or a user with App Marketplace access, in the profile's owners and book the approval.

rules.reason: ZDR turns off cloud sessions, so this highly sensitive scheduled task must run in the customer's own environment on a managed device, not in Anthropic's cloud.
rules.fix: Run the scheduled task in the customer's own environment on a managed device, not in Anthropic's cloud, and say so in the build.

rules.reason: The HIPAA configuration turns off cloud sessions, so this PHI scheduled task must run in the customer's own environment on a managed device, not in Anthropic's cloud.
rules.fix: Run the scheduled task in the customer's own environment on a managed device under the HIPAA configuration, not in Anthropic's cloud, and say so in the build.

rules.reason: Highly sensitive data needs a separate Enterprise org with ZDR, and the profile's retention is not zdr, so it does not show one.
rules.fix: Confirm with the customer that a separate Enterprise org with ZDR holds this work and record it in the profile, or lower the task's data class with the customer's compliance owner.

rules.reason: The task reads a system on a private network, with no allowlisting and no MCP tunnel on this plan, so the system is reachable only from Claude Code running on a device inside the network (a local MCP server), not from chat or Cowork connectors and not from a cloud scheduled task.
rules.fix: Build the task for Claude Code on a device inside the network with a local MCP server for the system, or allowlist Anthropic's IP range 160.79.104.0/21 at the edge, or move to Enterprise for an MCP tunnel.

rules.reason: The role's devices are mixed: the people on managed devices use Claude Code on the ZDR or HIPAA sign-in, but the people on unmanaged devices get no direct access to this data class.
rules.fix: Give the people on unmanaged devices managed devices, or run a hosted twin on our infrastructure that their device only displays.

rules.reason: Page 10 requires custom retention for confidential data, and the profile's retention is standard.
rules.fix: On Enterprise, set custom retention for the org. On Team, where custom retention is not offered, record that the customer accepts standard retention, under which, page 10 says, "otherwise local sessions are kept 6 years".

rules.reason: Custom retention does not cover Claude Tag or Managed Agents, and this task runs on one of them, so the customer's 30-day setting does not reach its data.
rules.fix: Tell the customer custom retention does not reach this task, and agree its retention with them or move it to a runtime custom retention covers.

rules.reason: Tasks share a connector tool but want different settings for it, so both run at the stricter task's setting.
rules.fix: Split the tools (a separate connector or tool per task), or run both tasks at the stricter level.
